_note: The beat runner's script (cine/beats.gd, design/typical-day.md section 2). A sequence is an ordered list of beats. A beat starts by applying `allow` (player.allow: only these actions work; [] everything, ["none"] nothing, but every beat keeps `look`: the kid can always turn the view and the hero (skills/guided-tutorial row 1); names are input actions or their family, move and look; a beat without `allow` keeps the last one; the sequence's end allows everything), running `do`, giving PIP its `pip` order, emitting its `task` (a line id for the Today list, kept until the next one), its `objective` ("pip", a landmark or an item id; null clears it) and its `line` (an id the HUD looks up) with opts {keys: `keys`, fact: `fact`}, unlocking its `page` (a handbook page id or a list of them: page(id) once each) and offering its `check` ({id, q, options, right, pages}: check_offered(check); the beat then needs no `wait`, it ends on checked:<id>), then waits; when `wait` is met (or after `max_s`) it emits beat_done(id) and the next beat starts, or the one named in `then` ("end" stops the sequence). wait: {time: s} | {place: {at, r}} (the hero within r m of a spot) | {action: name or [names]} | {event: name or [names]} (a list waits for all); `fact: true` also waits for "dismissed" (the HUD's Enter or tap). Actions and events all arrive through notify(name): jump and look (the view turned look_deg) are watched by the runner, and so are move_forward, move_back, move_left, move_right and hurry (held hold_s, hurry only while really hurrying); lift and use:<what> come from the interactions, pip_arrived from PIP, chose:<id> from the rules, dismissed, checked:<id>, map_open and map_closed from the HUD, shot_done:<name> from the cinematics. PIP says a beat's line once and is quiet while the kid is on the step (nearer its place by 1 m, a watched key held, the view turning, beside the leading PIP). A beat with a job for the kid (keys, an objective, a follow_me or `nag`; never a fact) reminds twice at most: after each of nag.at_s seconds without progress PIP says nag.lines (or the beat's own `nag` ids; while it leads, pip.call_line) with the beat's keys and a sound, the beat's line comes back after back_s, and after the last one PIP says no more in that beat. pip: go_to (drive and park; wave and point_at then happen on arrival), follow_me (lead there at the hero's pace: full speed while the hero is within lead_near_m, slowing to a stop at lead_wait_m, going on within lead_resume_m), point_at (stop and look), wave. While the beats hold PIP, a hero walking into it makes it back off once within back_m plus back_lead_s seconds of the hero's closing speed (at most back_s). do: clock:dawn (jump the look to dawn and pin it), clock:<hour> (put the look at that hour of this sol and pin it), clock:run (let it run), clock:skip (the time-lapse to the next phase), open:<item> (open its door), close:<item> (shut it, interactions.set_door), shot:<name> (a camera shot: dawn_reveal, focus_pip, look_around), hero:<start> (put the hero at a `starts` row), walk:<spot> (the hero walks there on its own at walk speed through the real controller, input still blocked; the spot as "x,z" or an id; it ends with the beat, so wait on the place), ghost:on|off (the Earth jump beside the hero), offer:<choice id> (choice_offered; the rules own it), apply:<choice id>, event:<event id> and report:<id> (rule(<the whole command>): the root hands a choice to the rules' apply, starts a rules event, shows the report card). A spot is [x, z], a PIP stop id (world.json pip.stops), a landmark, an item id, `pip` or `hero`; a look point is [x, z, height], a stop id (its look), an item id or `hero`. All numbers here are art direction. The opening wakes at clock:5.8, pre-dawn (the sun 3 deg under the horizon, blue twilight, not night): the sun clears the crater rim at about 06:08 seen from dawn_reveal's wide view (cine.gd sunrise_hour()), and the shot runs the clock on so it breaks over the rim while the kid watches, however slowly the walk-out went (the walk is automatic). At the old clock:dawn (06:19) the sun was already 3 deg over the rim

outdoors._note: a beat with outdoors: true (an outdoor shot) starts only with the hero out of every room and clear_m from every door; until then PIP leads the way out to spot [x, z] (skills/guided-tutorial row 3)

ghost._note: the faint hero beside the real one doing the same hop on Earth (cine/beats_ghost.gd): color a DESIGN.md token, alpha its opacity, side_m to the hero's right, linger_s shown after it lands (the hero is still in the air for about 0.4 s of it)

airlock._note: inside HAB 1, at its door, facing out, clear of the hatch's inward swing (item space; the model's door is on its -Z front)

opening._note: Sol 1 starts here, with no script (Ravindu, 14 Nov: 'ditch both hard coded animations ... user goes outside, and enjoy the sunrise'): the hero wakes in HAB 1's airlock facing the open hatch, which faces the sunrise (data/world.json hab1 yaw), with move and look free from the first frame. The clock runs from the first frame too; the root starts it so the sun's first sliver clears the rim about 45 s after the cover lifts (data/cine.json opening). The beat ends once the kid is out. PIP waits at [10.048, -1.503] from the first frame (pip.place, then go_to): 8 m out from HAB 1's hatch (its inner face, HAB 1's own [0, -2.16], here [2.133, -0.338]) along the sun's bearing at the opening's hour (81.6 deg at 05:25, cine.dawn_hour(); the door faces 81), so a kid looking straight out of the hatch has PIP in the middle of the frame with the dawn behind it, not off to the left at the airlock stop (15 Nov). World numbers: if the base turns again they go stale, and tests/beats_test.gd fails until they are derived again
a teaching line never stops the game (design/plans/mission-1-contracts.md): it shows for its time while the kid plays on, and its page keeps the fact in the handbook
the three meters, one line each, said once, as soon as the kid can move (15 Nov playtest: 'we don't really know what our 3 indicators do'); the page keeps them. Teaching lines: the game never stops
the tour: PIP leads to each thing the day's check and choice are about and says one line there
the sol's one question, asked once its three pages were shown; it ends on checked:sol1 (the HUD's card), never on a time

the kid's own needs start here (apply:body_on, the rules' knob `body`; nothing of the body ticks before it), and PIP leads home. Then hands on, each with its waypoint and each waiting for the use itself: suit air, a drink, a meal, all in HAB 1 (data/world.json uses), whose hatch the airlock opens. The numbers stay on the pages (rows 135, 254, 25, 188)
the kid stands in HAB 1 by now, beside the bed: PIP says the work is done and nobody is led anywhere

nag._note: PIP's quiet rules (design/plans/mission-1.md section 2). A beat's line is said once. at_s: one reminder at each of these seconds without progress (nearer the place by 1 m, a watched key held, the view turning, beside the leading PIP), then none for that beat. Its lines by reminder (`lines` for a key step, `place_lines` for a step that waits on a place: only there does 'Over here!' fit; a leading PIP says pip.call_line) and sounds by reminder (audio.gd SOUNDS names). An aside, a reminder or a call gives way to the beat's own line after back_s

offers._note: Each choice a beat offers (offer:<id>): the card's title line id, its options (text line id, the rules sim choices it applies, and the `gain` and `lose` line ids that say in words what those rules do to the meters). No number on a card without a factcheck row (workspace hard rule 3).

sol5_storm._note: apply is empty on purpose: the root halves the dose while the hero stands in the shelter (sandbox.gd, shelter_in and shelter_out by the hero's room), so a rule set here would fight it. The kid's own place and hands make the choice real: stay inside, or go out and brush the wings
